did_you_know.text: Did you know that Amos addresses both the people of Zion and those who trust in Mount Samaria, condemning their sense of security and superiority?
Did you know that Amos mentions Calneh, Hamath Rabbah, and Gath of the Philistines, and suggests comparing their condition with that of the kingdoms of Israel and Judah?
Did you know that Amos accuses the people of pushing away and dismissing the thought of the day of disaster, thereby bringing violent conduct closer?
Did you know that the description of luxurious living includes beds of ivory, reclining in comfort, eating lambs from the flock, and calves from the stall?
Did you know that the wealthy people described in the chapter play musical instruments and regard themselves as composers like David?
Did you know that the feast includes drinking wine from bowls and anointing themselves with the finest oils, yet despite all this abundance, they do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph?
Did you know that the contrast between a life of luxury and indifference to Joseph’s ruin leads to a sentence of exile, and that they will be among the first to go into exile?
Did you know that the Lord swears by himself that he detests the pride of Jacob and hates his palaces, and therefore will give the city and everything in it over to destruction?
Did you know that the chapter describes a situation in which, even if ten people remain in one house, they will all die?

Did you know that the chapter ends with an image of a society in which justice and righteousness have been turned into something destructive, and then announces that a nation will rise to oppress Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah?
